blocks.text: Living in Grandview Heights, South Surrey
Living in Grandview Heights, South Surrey

parts.t: Grandview Heights is a South Surrey neighbourhood that has changed a lot since the City approved its land use plan in 2005. Former farms and acreages have become townhome complexes and newer single-family streets, with Grandview Corners for shopping, a 50-metre aquatic centre and three new schools opened since 2021. Because so much is still being built, what is planned next to a home matters as much as the home.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.

parts.t: Grandview Heights is planned in pieces, so the plan for a specific lot, and for the lots around it, tells you most of what you need to know.
The Grandview Heights General Land Use Plan was approved in June 2005. It covers about 1,050 hectares from 16 Avenue to 28 Avenue, with

Detailed Neighbourhood Concept Plans guide each area. As of 2026 the City reports Morgan Heights is almost complete, Sunnyside Heights and Orchard Grove are under development, and Redwood Heights and Darts Hill are waiting for sewer and water servicing.
Grandview Heights Area 5 does not have a plan yet. The City started planning it in 2026, with a draft land use plan expected in early 2027.
Provincial SSMUH (small-scale multi-unit housing) rules also apply to single-family lots.
Before you buy, check the plan designation for the lot and the vacant or older lots around it.

Is there farmland (ALR) near Grandview Heights?

Yes. The Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) runs along the east side of Grandview Heights, and the City’s plan calls for buffers where new housing backs onto it. ALR land has its own rules on homes, subdivision and land use, set by the Agricultural Land Commission. If a lot is on or next to the ALR, check it on the
and ask what it means for the property before you buy.
What kind of homes are in Grandview Heights?
Mostly townhome complexes and newer single-family homes, plus some condos and older homes on acreage. Most streets were built after the first neighbourhood plan was approved in 2005.

Grandview Heights Secondary (opened 2021) serves most of the area, but some southern addresses are in the Earl Marriott Secondary catchment. Elementary schools include Edgewood (2021), Ta’talu (2024) and École Pacific Heights. Catchments have changed as new schools opened, so confirm the exact address with the
What is being built in Grandview Heights?

The area is planned through the Grandview Heights General Land Use Plan and several Neighbourhood Concept Plans. The City reports Sunnyside Heights and Orchard Grove are under development, Redwood Heights and Darts Hill are waiting for servicing, and Area 5 is being planned now. Check the plan for the lots around any home you are considering.
Is there a pool or recreation centre?
at 16855 24 Avenue has a 10-lane 50-metre pool, a leisure pool and dive towers up to 10 metres.
Grandview Corners, around 24 Avenue and 160 Street, is the main shopping area, with Morgan Crossing nearby.
